BiblicalUsage: The word hallâz carries the sense of this or that, on this side or that. In 1 Samuel 14:1, the text says "that [is] on the other side. But he told not his father." The word keeps that same sense wherever it appears.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hallâz shows us that hope is not wishing; it is trusting God for what He has promised, even before we see it. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Gideon's Victory over Midian; Elisha and the Shunammite's Son; Jonathan's Victory at Michmash
